sentences.text: Kayleigh Morris is the mother of a 12-day-old infant named Ruby.
The health visitor is Bethan Lloyd.
The visit is a new birth visit for Ruby, who is 12 days old.
Kayleigh's partner, Dean, is at work during the visit and returns around 3 PM.
Dean works early shifts at a warehouse.
Kayleigh and Dean have a tense relationship due to lack of sleep.
Kayleigh has not seen her mother since September, before Ruby was born.
Kayleigh's mother has not met Ruby.
Kayleigh registered Ruby's birth on the day before the visit.
Kayleigh is breastfeeding Ruby primarily, with one bottle of formula given at night.
Ruby is fed every two to two and a half hours during the day, with occasional cluster feeding.
Ruby has six to seven wet nappies per day.
Ruby's birth weight was 3.2 kg as recorded by the midwife on day five.
Ruby's current weight is 3.41 kg, measured at the time of the visit.
Kayleigh reports that her physical recovery postpartum is 'bit sore still but better'.
Kayleigh reports that her mood is 'up and down' and that she 'cries a lot'.
Dean pushed Kayleigh into a wardrobe door during an argument, which occurred three to four times since summer.
Dean punched Kayleigh in the stomach during pregnancy in August, at approximately 30 weeks gestation.
Kayleigh did not report any further physical harm from Dean during pregnancy.
Dean checks Kayleigh's phone every night and goes mad if she messages someone he does not like.
Dean has never hurt or been rough with Ruby.
Kayleigh feels safe at home during the visit because Dean is at work.
Kayleigh's GP, Dr Anand, will be informed about the safeguarding concerns.
Kayleigh is willing to receive a referral to Harbridge Women's Aid, an outreach service, which will call her sister Kirsty's number when Dean is at work.
Kayleigh will provide the number 077 for the outreach service to use.
Kayleigh has applied for child benefit but does not currently have her own bank card.
The health visitor will refer Kayleigh to Harbridge Women's Aid and the referral will be made on the same day.
The outreach service will call Kayleigh's sister Kirsty's phone by Friday.
The health visitor will speak to the safeguarding lead and inform the GP about the concerns on the same day.
The health visitor will return on Thursday, 3rd December, at 11 AM when Dean is at work.
